resources.string: Heatmap • Time per deck • Leaderboard • RWKV • Updates
A year or a month of reviews done and cards due, below the decks
The time answered today on each deck row
Signed in as %s. Off hides the board and stops the uploads; the sign-in is kept.
The Anki Leaderboard add-on\'s board (an unofficial client of its server). Sign in from the deck list menu.
Lofi music while you study: tap the headphones in the deck list or the reviewer, long-press for tracks, volume and sources

Under \'Studied today\': review cards due, added by the daily minimum, near the line and safe now, and how many more become due in 1 h, 3 h and by tomorrow. Not shown above 3000 review cards (too slow)
Below the heatmap: a dot per review card at its recall now, coloured like the forecast\'s counts. Not shown above 3000 review cards either
Shown when the RWKV state is rebuilt (first start, after an update), and a notification when it is ready

%s. Big: the desktop fork\'s model. Small: JSchoreels\' 331k-parameter model, about 0.7%% less accurate (log loss, 1,000 held-out users), with about a quarter of the memory and rebuilds about 3x faster: a 4M-review, 100k-card collection rebuilds in under 1 GB, where the big model needs 2.6 GB. A change rebuilds the RWKV state from the review history

%s. How each card\'s RWKV memory is kept, as in the desktop fork: int8 uses about a third of f32\'s memory with the same accuracy; int4 cards / int8 notes a quarter less than int8, slightly less accurate. A change rebuilds the RWKV state from the review history
After Show answer, the answer buttons fade in (200 ms). Off: they appear at once
Once a day, asks GitHub for a newer kuma3 Anki release and offers to install it
%s. Debug build: updates come from the PC (adb)
kuma3 Anki is up to date
Allow kuma3 Anki to install updates, then come back: the update is offered again
